question_text:
Give plausible explanation for each of the following:
(i) Cyclohexanone forms cyanohydrin in good yield but 2, 2, 6 trimethylcyclohexanone does not.
(ii) There are two -NH groups in semicarbazide. However, only one is involved in the formation of semicarbazones.
(iii) During the preparation of esters from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst, the water or the ester should be removed as soon as it is formed.

question_image.description: Chemical structures and reactions related to the formation of cyanohydrins and semicarbazones.

parts.part_text: Cyclohexanone forms cyanohydrin in good yield but 2, 2, 6 trimethylcyclohexanone does not.
parts.answer_text: Cyclohexanone can easily undergo nucleophilic attack by CN- due to less steric hindrance, while in 2, 2, 6 trimethylcyclohexanone, the methyl groups create steric hindrance preventing effective attack.

steps.description: Identify the steric hindrance in 2, 2, 6 trimethylcyclohexanone.
Explain how steric hindrance affects nucleophilic attack.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, cyclohexanone forms cyanohydrin while 2, 2, 6 trimethylcyclohexanone does not due to steric hindrance.

parts.part_text: There are two -NH groups in semicarbazide. However, only one is involved in the formation of semicarbazones.
parts.answer_text: Only one -NH group participates in resonance with the carbonyl group, reducing its nucleophilicity, while the other -NH group remains free to act as a nucleophile.

steps.description: Identify the -NH groups in semicarbazide.
Explain the resonance effect on nucleophilicity.

parts.final_answer: Thus, only one -NH group is involved in forming semicarbazones.

parts.part_text: During the preparation of esters from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst, the water or the ester should be removed as soon as it is formed.
parts.answer_text: Removing water or ester shifts the equilibrium towards ester formation, preventing the reverse reaction.

steps.description: Explain the reversible nature of ester formation.
Discuss the effect of removing products on equilibrium.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, to maximize ester production, water or ester must be removed promptly.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of chemical reactions and mechanisms.

question_text: Although phenoxide ion has more number of resonating structures than carboxylate ion, carboxylic acid is a stronger acid than phenol. Why?
answer_text: Carboxylic acid is a stronger acid than phenol because the resonance structures of carboxylate ion contribute more towards its stability than those of phenoxide ion.

steps.description: Analyze the resonance structures of phenoxide ion and carboxylate ion.
Identify that in phenoxide ion, some structures have negative charge on less electronegative carbon atoms, contributing less to stability.
Note that in carboxylate ion, the negative charge is delocalized over two electronegative oxygen atoms, enhancing stability.

final_answer: Thus, carboxylic acid is a stronger acid than phenol due to greater resonance stabilization of the carboxylate ion.
